title: eSIM explained: a SIM card you download
description: An eSIM is a chip soldered into your phone that holds downloadable carrier profiles. Here's how it replaces the plastic card.

scenes.big: An eSIM is a SIM you download
scenes.say: That tiny SIM card tray might be disappearing. In its place is a chip already inside your phone.
A normal SIM is a removable card that proves to a carrier that your phone may join its network. An eSIM is a chip soldered into the phone. Your identity is a software profile, not a piece of plastic.
The chip's technical name is eUICC. The industry body GSMA defines an eSIM as a SIM with remote provisioning, meaning profiles can be installed over the air.

steps: Carrier gives you a QR code or app
scenes.say: To set one up, you usually scan a QR code from your carrier. The phone downloads your profile and installs it. Switching carriers means swapping a profile, not a card.
Many phones can hold more than one profile, so a home plan and a travel plan can sit side by side. Follow for more.
